source: Qudūrī — Intro to Qudūrī, class notes 2026-09-09

cards.front: What role does مُخْتَصَر القُدُورِي play for a student?
cards.back: The entry point into the Ḥanafī school of thought

cards.front: What is the stated purpose of مُخْتَصَر القُدُورِي?
cards.back: To present the relied-upon positions of the madhhab

cards.front: What does مُخْتَصَر القُدُورِي deliberately leave out, and what does that make it?
cards.back: It mentions no evidences — it is simply a manual of law

cards.meaning: linguistically — a definition by the word's ordinary language sense
technically — a definition by the term's specialist usage

cards.text: Scholars define a term two ways: {{c1::لُغَةً::linguistically}} and {{c2::اِصْطِلَاحًا::technically}}
For a definition to be sound it must be {{c1::مَانِع::excluding}} — excluding what does not belong — and {{c2::جَامِع::including}} — including everything that does

cards.meaning: preventive — a definition excludes whatever is not necessary to it
comprehensive — a definition includes everything necessary to it

cards.front: What does فِقْه mean لُغَةً?
cards.back: To understand and comprehend

cards.front: Who gave one of the first technical definitions of فِقْه, and what was it?
cards.back: Imām Abū Ḥanīfah — an individual knowing their rights and responsibilities

cards.text: Abū Ḥanīfah's definition of فِقْه: {{c1::مَعْرِفَةُ النَّفْسِ مَا لَهَا وَمَا عَلَيْهَا}}
cards.extra: an individual knowing their rights and responsibilities

cards.front: What is the problem with Abū Ḥanīfah's definition of فِقْه?
cards.back: It is very broad — it takes in ʿaqīdah and ādāb as well

cards.text: The refined definition of فِقْه: {{c1::الْعِلْمُ بِالْأَحْكَامِ الشَّرْعِيَّةِ}} {{c2::الْعَمَلِيَّةِ}} {{c3::الْمُكْتَسَبَةِ مِنْ أَدِلَّتِهَا التَّفْصِيلِيَّةِ}}
cards.extra: the knowledge of practical legal rulings derived from their detailed evidences

cards.front: Translate the refined definition of فِقْه.
cards.back: The knowledge of practical legal rulings derived from their detailed evidences

cards.front: In the definition of فِقْه, what do “the detailed evidences” refer to?
cards.back: The four sources of fiqh

cards.front: Name the four sources of فِقْه. (Q, S, I, Q)
cards.back: القُرْآن، السُّنَّة، الإِجْمَاع، القِيَاس

cards.front: What does “practical legal rulings” mean in the definition of فِقْه?
cards.back: The laws related to a person's actions or conduct

cards.front: What does the refined definition of فِقْه exclude, and to which science does that belong?
cards.back: Knowledge related to the articles of faith — that is the subject of ʿaqīdah

cards.text: The three categories of فِقْه: {{c1::عِبَادَات}}, {{c2::مُعَامَلَات}}, and {{c3::جِنَايَات}}

cards.meaning: rules and regulations of worship and its related actions, such as purification
commercial and interpersonal law, and judicial matters — adjudication, court procedure, evidence
crimes, offences, and their penalties — criminal law

cards.front: Which categories of فِقْه does القُدُورِي cover?
cards.back: All three — عِبَادَات، مُعَامَلَات، جِنَايَات

cards.front: What does شَرِيعَة mean لُغَةً?
cards.back: A watering hole or drinking place — where a person or animal comes to drink

cards.front: What does شَرِيعَة mean اِصْطِلَاحًا?
cards.back: What Allah has legislated for His servants from the religion — Allah's revealed code

cards.front: What is the شَرِيعَة for?
cards.back: It is what we follow to be guided in this world and to attain salvation

cards.front: What does the شَرِيعَة include?
cards.back: Creed, ritual acts of worship, morals, ethics, and law

cards.text: {{c1::فِقْه}} and {{c2::شَرِيعَة}} are often used interchangeably, but {{c3::شَرِيعَة}} is far the broader of the two

cards.front: What does شَرِيعَة take in that فِقْه does not?
cards.back: Creed, morals, and ethics — فِقْه is confined to practical legal rulings

cards.front: From which verb does مَذْهَب derive, and what does it mean?
cards.back: ذَهَبَ / يَذْهَبُ — to go, or to take as a way

cards.front: Grammatically, what two things can مَذْهَب be?
cards.back: Either a ظَرْف مَكَانِي or a مَصْدَر

cards.front: What does مَذْهَب mean لُغَةً?
cards.back: A way, course, or manner of acting; an opinion on a particular case; a doctrine; the opinion one chooses to adopt

cards.front: What does مَذْهَب mean اِصْطِلَاحًا?
cards.back: A legal school, or legal school of thought

cards.text: A مَذْهَب is a non-formal association of jurists sharing loyalty to {{c1::a particular set of legal precepts}} and {{c2::a particular methodology of interpretation and of deriving law}}

cards.front: Name the four extant مَذَاهِب. (Ḥ, M, Sh, Ḥ)
cards.back: حَنَفِي، مَالِكِي، شَافِعِي، حَنْبَلِي

cards.front: After whom is each مَذْهَب named?
cards.back: A master-jurist — a مُجْتَهِد قَطْعِي — to whom a particular methodology of deriving law is attributed

cards.front: Were there ever more than four مَذَاهِب?
cards.back: Yes — there used to be many more; these four were codified, preserved, and survived

cards.meaning: one who performs ijtihād — the master-jurist a madhhab is named for

cards.front: What is اِجْتِهَاد?
cards.back: The effort made to derive law, which is not self-evident, from the primary sources

cards.front: What does اِجْتِهَاد require of the one performing it?
cards.back: A great deal of skill and expertise across many subject areas

cards.text: A مَذْهَب is both {{c1::a framework for interpreting and deriving law from the Qurʾān and Sunnah}} and {{c2::the body of law that comes out of that framework}}

cards.front: Does following the Ḥanafī madhhab mean holding every opinion of Imām Abū Ḥanīfah?
cards.back: No — it is following the scholarly tradition that developed over time by adhering to the methodology of the founders

cards.front: Is following a مَذْهَب an objective in itself?
cards.back: No — it is a means to follow the Qurʾān in a reliable, systematic, methodical, and coherent manner

cards.front: What is the ruling on following a مَذْهَب?
cards.back: Not technically wājib or farḍ, but very highly encouraged

cards.front: In what sense does the average person not have a مَذْهَب?
cards.back: Their madhhab is that of the imam they go to with their questions

cards.front: Why should a student choose a مَذْهَب once they begin studying?
cards.back: To develop coherence and internal consistency

cards.front: Historically, what determined which مَذْهَب a person followed?
cards.back: Schools developed in particular regions; people followed the one they had access to

cards.front: What is Imām Abū Ḥanīfah's full name?
cards.back: النُّعْمَان بْن ثَابِت بْن زُوطَى بْن مَاه التَّيْمِي الكُوفِي

cards.front: Which part of Abū Ḥanīfah's full name is the part to know?
cards.back: النُّعْمَان بْن ثَابِت — Nuʿmān ibn Thābit

cards.meaning: the greatest Imām — Abū Ḥanīfah's honorific title

cards.front: Where and in what year was Abū Ḥanīfah born?
cards.back: In Kufa, Iraq, in the year 80

cards.front: Where and in what year did Abū Ḥanīfah die?
cards.back: In Baghdad, in the year 150

cards.front: What is Abū Ḥanīfah's place among the four Imāms?
cards.back: He is the first of them

cards.front: On what grounds do some consider Abū Ḥanīfah a تَابِعِي?
cards.back: He may have seen Anas ibn Mālik RA as a child

cards.front: At whose command was Kufa founded?
cards.back: ʿUmar RA

cards.front: Whose legacy made Kufa a major centre of learning?
cards.back: Ibn Masʿūd and ʿAlī raḍiyallāhu ʿanhumā

cards.front: How does Kufa rank for the number of Companions who settled there?
cards.back: More settled there than in any city apart from Makkah and Madinah

cards.front: Which Companions are named as the most prominent of those associated with Kufa?
cards.back: ʿUmar RA, ʿAlī RA, and Ibn Masʿūd RA

cards.front: How did the school of Kufa come into being?
cards.back: Out of the body of fiqh understanding that developed among the Companions and scholars who settled there

cards.front: What was Abū Ḥanīfah's family trade, and what did he do in his youth?
cards.back: A family of traders — he spent time as a silk merchant

cards.front: Who recognised Abū Ḥanīfah's ability and redirected him to studying?
cards.back: Imām al-Shaʿbī

cards.front: What did al-Shaʿbī advise Abū Ḥanīfah to do?
cards.back: To start studying Islam and sitting with the scholars

cards.front: Which field did Abū Ḥanīfah excel in before turning to fiqh?
cards.back: Theology

cards.front: In what year, and at what age, did Abū Ḥanīfah turn to fiqh?
cards.back: In the year 102, aged 22

cards.front: Who was Abū Ḥanīfah's principal teacher in fiqh, and what was his position?
cards.back: Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān — the chief jurist of Kufa

cards.front: For how long did Abū Ḥanīfah study with Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān?
cards.back: 18 years

cards.front: What did Ḥammād permit Abū Ḥanīfah to do?
cards.back: Give legal rulings on his behalf

cards.front: What happened when Ḥammād died in the year 120?
cards.back: Abū Ḥanīfah was offered his position, and reluctantly accepted

cards.front: How many scholars is Abū Ḥanīfah said to have studied with?
cards.back: Over 4,000

cards.text: Abū Ḥanīfah's fiqh lineage: he studied with {{c1::حَمَّاد بْن أَبِي سُلَيْمَان}}, who learned from {{c2::إِبْرَاهِيم النَّخَعِي}}, who learned from {{c3::عَلْقَمَة بْن قَيْس النَّخَعِي}}, who learned from {{c4::ابْن مَسْعُود}}
cards.extra: Four links back to a Companion.

cards.front: How did the madhāhib begin?
cards.back: As geographic schools — the understanding of the different scholars and Ṣaḥābah in different cities

cards.text: School origins: the Ḥanafī from {{c1::the school of Kufa}}; the Mālikī from {{c2::the school of Madinah}}; the Ḥanbalī from {{c3::ahl al-ḥadīth in Basra}}

cards.front: On what legacy is the Shāfiʿī school built?
cards.back: Makkah, then Madinah and Kufa, then later the ḥadīth movement in Iraq

cards.front: When and where did the school of ahl al-ḥadīth develop?
cards.back: In the later half of the second century, in Basra

cards.front: What did ahl al-ḥadīth want to do with ijtihād and qiyās?
cards.back: Minimise them — not eliminate them

cards.front: For how long did Abū Ḥanīfah teach fiqh and give fatāwā?
cards.back: Thirty years

cards.front: What need did Abū Ḥanīfah recognise in the fiqh of his time?
cards.back: For a structured, systematic, organised approach that had not existed before

cards.front: What body did Abū Ḥanīfah form, and of how many?
cards.back: A committee of 40 jurists

cards.front: What was Abū Ḥanīfah's own role in the committee's daily debates?
cards.back: He would listen to the discussion, summarise it, then offer his own conclusions and opinions

cards.front: What was the committee's goal, and what happened when it could not be reached?
cards.back: Unanimity and consensus — where differences could not be reconciled, the differing opinions were recorded

cards.front: Over what period did the committee work, and to what extent?
cards.back: Thirty years, deciding thousands of issues

cards.front: Complete the famous statement about him: “You jurists are doctors and we are the pharmacists, and you are …”
cards.back: …a man who has got hold of both sides

cards.front: What did Abū Ḥanīfah refuse to do?
cards.back: Serve the rulers and sultans of his time

cards.front: What was the consequence of that refusal?
cards.back: He was placed under house arrest near the end of his life

cards.front: Did house arrest stop Abū Ḥanīfah teaching?
cards.back: No — it did not prevent him from teaching others

cards.front: In which month did Abū Ḥanīfah die?
cards.back: Rajab

cards.front: What was the cause of Abū Ḥanīfah's death?
cards.back: Poison administered by prison guards, on the command of the Abbasid caliph Manṣūr

cards.front: How many times was Abū Ḥanīfah's funeral prayer performed, and by how many?
cards.back: Six times — more than 50,000 people prayed over him

cards.front: Name Abū Ḥanīfah's four main students. (Z, AY, M, H)
cards.back: زُفَر، أَبُو يُوسُف، مُحَمَّد، الحَسَن بْن زِيَاد

cards.front: What is Zufar's full name?
cards.back: زُفَر بْن الهُذَيْل

cards.front: In which two fields was Zufar a scholar?
cards.back: Both fiqh and ḥadīth

cards.front: In what three fields was Abū Yūsuf a specialist?
cards.back: Ḥadīth, tafsīr, and the history of the Arabs

cards.front: What is Muḥammad's full name?
cards.back: مُحَمَّد بْن الحَسَن الشَّيْبَانِي

cards.front: Which two students are called the pillars of the madhhab?
cards.back: Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan

cards.front: With whom did Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan continue after Abū Ḥanīfah died?
cards.back: Abū Yūsuf

cards.front: Which of the four Imāms did Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan teach?
cards.back: Imām al-Shāfiʿī

cards.front: Which of Imām Mālik's works did Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrate?
cards.back: The Muwaṭṭaʾ

cards.meaning: an absolute mujtahid — one who derives law independently; Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan was one, though out of respect he attributed his work to Abū Ḥanīfah
the six books of Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan — considered the backbone of the madhhab

cards.front: Whose opinions did Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan compile in ظَاهِر الرِّوَايَة?
cards.back: The well-established opinions of Abū Ḥanīfah, his own, and Abū Yūsuf's

cards.text: Years studied with Abū Ḥanīfah — Zufar {{c1::over 20}}; Abū Yūsuf {{c2::over 17}}; Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan {{c3::2}}
cards.extra: Four similar durations sit in this section; holding them in one view is what keeps them apart.

cards.front: What is Imām al-Qudūrī's full name?
cards.back: أَبُو الحَسَن أَحْمَد بْن مُحَمَّد القُدُورِي

cards.front: In what year was Imām al-Qudūrī born?
cards.back: 973 (CE — see draft)

cards.front: In what year did Imām al-Qudūrī die?
cards.back: 1037 (CE — see draft)

cards.front: What is Imām al-Qudūrī's standing among Ḥanafī scholars?
cards.back: He is considered among the leading ones

cards.front: What does مُخْتَصَر mean, and what does that imply about the book?
cards.back: An abridgment — it is itself derived from much more comprehensive books

cards.text: فَرْض: {{c1::مَا ثَبَتَ بِدَلِيلٍ قَطْعِيٍّ}} {{c2::لَا شُبْهَةَ فِيهِ}}
cards.extra: That which is established by a definitive proof, in which there is no doubt.

cards.front: What is a فَرْض, in the Ḥanafī legal values?
cards.back: An act established by a definitive proof which is not open to interpretation

cards.front: What counts as a definitive proof for a فَرْض?
cards.back: A verse of the Qurʾān, or a mutawātir ḥadīth

cards.text: سُنَّة مُؤَكَّدَة: {{c1::مَا وَاظَبَ عَلَيْهِ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ}} {{c2::مَعَ تَرْكِهِ أَحْيَانًا}}
cards.extra: What the Prophet ﷺ persisted in, while leaving it on occasion.

cards.front: Translate the definition of سُنَّة مُؤَكَّدَة.
cards.back: What the Prophet ﷺ persisted in, while leaving it on occasion

cards.text: سُنَّة غَيْر مُؤَكَّدَة: {{c1::مَا فَعَلَهُ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ مَرَّةً}} {{c2::وَتَرَكَهُ أُخْرَى}}
cards.extra: What the Prophet ﷺ did at one time and left at another.

cards.front: Translate the definition of سُنَّة غَيْر مُؤَكَّدَة.
cards.back: What the Prophet ﷺ did at one time and left at another

cards.text: In a {{c1::مُؤَكَّدَة}} sunnah the Prophet ﷺ {{c2::persisted in it, leaving it only occasionally}}; in a {{c3::غَيْر مُؤَكَّدَة}} sunnah he {{c4::did it at times and left it at others}}
cards.extra: Both definitions mention doing and leaving — the difference is which one was the norm.

cards.meaning: to persist in, to do consistently — the word that makes a sunnah مُؤَكَّدَة
